# Initial findings — 2026-11-08

## Repository observations

- [MatchesControllerTest](../../../../test/controllers/matches_controller_test.rb) inherits from `ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest` and contains 43 `assert_select` calls. Coverage includes layout text, board controls, hidden parameters, defaults, error alerts, history, and pagination.
- [ApplicationHelperTest](../../../../test/helpers/application_helper_test.rb) has four `assert_select` calls. These existing assertions are outside the agreed migration scope.
- [Test setup](../../../../test/test_helper.rb) loads Rails testing and parallelizes tests. It has no Capybara setup.
- [Gemfile](../../../../Gemfile) has neither Capybara nor the accessible-selectors gem.
- [ApplicationHelper](../../../../app/helpers/application_helper.rb) currently includes the component kit only.
- [Layout](../../../../app/views/layouts/application.html.haml) exposes the edition through a typography component with presentation classes.
- [Board](../../../../app/views/matches/_board.html.haml) already has translated accessible labels. Rails `button_to` owns action and hidden position/revision parameters.
- [Setup fields](../../../../app/views/matches/_setup_fields.html.haml) use Rails form helpers and existing labels.
- [History items](../../../../app/views/matches/_history_item.html.haml) have record-specific accessible link labels but no shared test hooks.
- [Component base](../../../../app/components/design_system/base.rb) accepts arbitrary HTML attributes. Data-hook forwarding needs verification in the implementation slice.
- The [composition guide](../../rails-view-composition/composition-guide.md) prohibits test-only CSS classes. The agreed data-attribute approach avoids that conflict; its documentation should explicitly distinguish the two.

## Upstream observations

The [upstream README](https://github.com/citizensadvice/capybara_accessible_selectors/blob/main/README.md) describes selectors based on labels and screen-reader-compatible markup, plus extensions to built-in Capybara selectors.

Its installation example uses a test-group Git dependency pinned to a release tag and warns that the main branch may contain breaking changes. Select an appropriate compatible release during implementation rather than treating the example as a verified dependency choice.

The GitHub page fetch timed out. Reading the raw upstream README succeeded. No gem was installed, and runtime compatibility has not been tested.

## Verification status

- `git --no-pager status --short`: clean before initiative setup.
- Counts and findings above come from source inspection, not executed application tests.
- Application tests, lint, builds, dependency resolution, and browser checks were not run during planning.

## Consequences

The migration can retain Rails request execution and add Capybara response assertions without a browser. Visibility behavior and response freshness require focused tests; replacing selector syntax alone is not sufficient.
